cards.title: Check jack vs king jambs and facing
cards.notes: QC-05 intentionally splits inner jamb around the header. It is not Revit auto-join trimming. All 343 mock members have joins disabled at both ends and exact web cut lengths. Saturday review, 30 minutes: use the existing disposable mock. This is the first human geometry gate.
cards.acceptance: Open QC-05: jack 84⅜ in, upper piece 31¾ in, outer king 119⅞ in. Compare QC-02's bearing arrangement. Check both window sides and C/T openings. Record any wrong member ID and screenshot.
cards.evidence: Live Revit 2023 readback, 2026-10-12; native join audit

cards.title: Approve opening framing combinations
cards.notes: Sixteen supported mock recipes exist. Automated cut/facing/gap checks pass; engineering and visible detailing approval remains yours.
cards.acceptance: Sunday review, 45 minutes: check single/boxed/double headers, doubled jambs, sill ends and door bottom track behavior. Confirm the current compact allowance summary and Original / R.O. sizes. Record bearing/seat intent; unsupported variants need their own binding. No requirement to restore the superseded four-side arrows.
cards.evidence: 343-member combination mock; 24 measured top gaps

cards.title: Try custom studs, jambs and bad edits
cards.notes: Three real UI panels exported 95 members; 34 stress variants produced 12 ready and 22 correctly blocked cases. New custom-axis native placement is still a separate gate. Saturday review, 30 minutes. Record custom member expectations before native placement.
cards.acceptance: Copy a stud, shorten it to 60 in, mirror a jamb and Undo. Confirm Sketch, cuts and PDF agree. Invalid length, opening collisions and missing supports must block release. Record expected behavior before native custom-axis placement.
cards.evidence: Real browser handlers at 1366 and 380 px; custom stress suite

cards.title: Confirm Revit template and gap inputs
cards.notes: The web accepts explicit normalized Revit settings with source labels and web overrides. The real exporter mapping has not shipped. Saturday review, 30 minutes after the native read-only bridge is available. Remains Planned until prerequisites pass.
cards.acceptance: After mapping is available, export a model wall with template name, gap, cutback, seating and end rules. Confirm inch conversion once, explicit zero/false, reload and Use Revit values. Confirm top gap replaces only top cutback.
cards.evidence: Version 1 revit.framingSettings contract

cards.title: Run complete workflow and scale acceptance
cards.notes: Sunday acceptance, 60 minutes on the packaged candidate. Require writer, recovery, two-user and scale evidence first. Existing 343-member mock timing does not qualify thousands of walls.
cards.acceptance: Load native source -> shared web resolve -> native change preview -> Apply -> independent Compare -> one sheet per panel and same QR/plain labels. Retry creates no duplicates. Update only CAS-owned members. Stop a large job at a panel boundary, retain completed panels, then resume safely. Check measured 100/1,000-wall evidence and record release blockers.
cards.evidence: Depends on writer, scale and release QA cards

cards.title: Approve the 45-day pilot and explicit support limits
cards.notes: Day 45 is an evidence-based release decision. Unavailable Revit versions, failed host combinations or unapproved recipes stay outside the pilot.
cards.acceptance: Review the support matrix and every open high-priority finding. Approve the actual tested scope or extend the affected gate. Record remaining limitations and next owners. November 26 may be a holiday; the sign-off can be asynchronous. A date alone never closes a failed test.
cards.evidence: Pilot target: October 13 through November 26, inclusive

cards.title: Map native template parameters into web input
cards.notes: Identify actual readable template, deflection, cutback and end-rule parameters. Preserve explicit values and source identity; MWF fields remain read-only.
cards.acceptance: Reviewed mapping with missing/invalid values blocked or clearly absent. Prove real export → browser consumption and override restoration.
cards.evidence: Existing web source settings support

cards.title: Build verified single-panel resolved-plan Apply
cards.notes: Bounded writer in CAS_FRAMING DEV, initially driven by reviewed JSON. Use authoritative physical axes/cuts and disjoin both ends. UI-host integration is separate; no duplicated framing engine.
cards.acceptance: Preflight exact features, source and family binding; create only CAS-owned members. Check actual transaction results. Independently verify final cuts, axes, facing, top gap and joins while rollback is still possible, including commit-time effects inside a rollback-capable group. Write ownership and receipt with the panel changes. Failed verification leaves zero partial members; one successful small Apply has one Undo action. Regeneration corruption aborts the job immediately.
cards.evidence: Mock prototype proves 343 members, not production import

cards.title: Place custom-axis members in the native mock
cards.notes: Custom sketch geometry is verified in the web. Translation of custom physical axes into actual Revit members has not been qualified.
cards.acceptance: Place the three reviewed synthetic cases, read back cut length/axis/facing/identity, preserve quantities, then inspect short studs and extra jambs.
cards.evidence: Requires custom review; disposable model

cards.title: Qualify generation for thousands of walls
cards.notes: Native mock: 343 members in roughly 19 seconds including audit. No thousand-wall claim. Web has bounded template caching and async yields.
cards.acceptance: Measure 100 and 1,000-wall synthetic generation, verification, payload size, memory and UI stalls separately; use 5,000 only after those pass. Test repeated templates and mixed recipes. Tune batch size from results, preserve quantities, stop between panels, and resume without duplicates. Establish and record acceptable timings with the owner; do not claim arbitrary millisecond or memory caps from the reports as proven.
cards.evidence: Existing web benchmark and live 343-member timing

cards.title: Decide unsupported header and slope details
cards.notes: Nested tracks, single-C header arrangement, native sloped end cuts and sloped deflection datum require approved physical details.
cards.acceptance: Record accepted diagrams/datums or defer each recipe. Default pilot excludes QC-08/09/17/18 until exact native arrangements pass. Keep unsupported Apply blocked, with an explicit reason. Do not substitute geometry or change fabrication tolerances to make a case pass.
cards.evidence: Combination mock skipped four recipes

cards.title: Connect the qualified local web workspace to Revit
cards.notes: Use the host selected in #028 with the same versioned local web bundle and a narrow transport-independent bridge. Model data stays local. Revit API work runs only through a valid ExternalEvent context.
cards.acceptance: Read selection, refresh source, locate, compare and save through versioned commands with schema, size, origin/peer, document and session checks. Reject stale or switched-document requests. Revit objects stay inside the adapter; background work gets DTOs only. Keep Apply disabled until #008/#031/#032 pass. Confirm actual keyboard, window and document lifecycle, not just compilation.
cards.evidence: Host feasibility proposal; not implemented

cards.title: Choose persistent shared board storage
cards.notes: Deferred infrastructure option: the bookmark board and browser drafts plus JSON sharing remain sufficient for this pilot. Review whether authenticated shared storage is actually needed after pilot feedback.
cards.acceptance: Record a proceed/defer decision with a concrete collaboration need and privacy requirements. Do not activate a new backend, tracking service or dependency merely for the plan.
cards.evidence: No new service or dependency required today

cards.title: Trial the workflow with a nontechnical user
cards.notes: Saturday nontechnical pilot, 30 minutes with a colleague. Record time, errors and where coaching was needed.
cards.acceptance: Without coaching, load a native panel, read source/template/gap origins, find a blocked issue, review proposed changes, apply one supported panel and save its sheet and labels. Distinguish web draft Undo from Revit Undo. Record confusing wording and report reproducible failures.
cards.evidence: Aim for one clear action at each stage

cards.title: Run final regression and host compatibility checks
cards.panel: Supported web and native release scope
cards.notes: Release gates must distinguish unit/build checks from actual host and visual proof.
cards.acceptance: Keep all frozen fixtures and quantities intact. Replay real desktop/narrow handlers, PDF/QR output and actual Revit operations. Qualify exact Revit patch/runtime/add-in/family combinations, including 2025.5/2026.5 .NET 10 where in the pilot fleet. Check document switching, stale requests, borrowed elements, failure, cancellation, Undo/Redo and unsupported rejection. Unsupported or unavailable hosts remain excluded, not marked passed.
cards.evidence: Depends on planned native writer and user reviews

cards.title: Publish month plan and Kanban review workflow
cards.notes: Replace planning categories with Planned, In progress, Your review and Done. Compact cards reveal detailed checks and result fields on click.
cards.acceptance: Drag cards, change owner/date/status with keyboard, filter your tests, reload drafts, import/export JSON and verify live URLs at 1366 and 380 px. No homepage link.
cards.evidence: 306 unit tests; real local and cloud-mode handlers at 1366/380 px; public URLs recorded in the web handoff

cards.title: Top gap replaces top cutback
cards.notes: Studs reaching top track use the web top gap instead of an additional top cutback. Lower ends retain allowance; slope/manual unsupported combinations stay blocked.
cards.acceptance: 24 live top gaps match 0.5 or 1 inch. Preserve this datum in every native binding.
cards.evidence: User direction and live gap readback

cards.title: Preserve fabrication numbers and quantities
cards.notes: Display dimensions round to nearest ⅛ inch; cut lengths floor to ⅛ inch intentionally. Physical resolved quantities are authoritative.
cards.acceptance: 23 frozen fixture outputs remain unchanged. No automatic quantity repair.
cards.evidence: Framing contract and frozen fixtures

cards.title: Verify 343 native mock cuts and facing
cards.notes: All 343 mock cuts match web output; facing vectors and 24 top-gap measures pass. This proves supported mock geometry, not a production writer or engineering approval.
cards.acceptance: Independent readback; zero allowed joins across 686 ends on October 12. User visual review is tracked separately.
cards.evidence: Live Revit 2023 audit

cards.title: Verify three Sketch panels and stress variants
cards.notes: Real-handler web tests and actual three-sheet PDF pass; added physical bounds, collisions, support checks and independent copied jamb identity.
cards.acceptance: 95 exported members; 34 stress cases; desktop/narrow; no fixture changes.
cards.evidence: 305 web tests at previous milestone

cards.title: Consume explicit Revit framing settings
cards.notes: Versioned inch values, template context and source origin supported. Web overrides survive reload and source restoration.
cards.acceptance: Explicit zero and false preserved; malformed unit/version/value rejected. Native exporter mapping remains Planned.
cards.evidence: Real browser source-settings handlers

cards.title: Disable framing joins and verify exact cuts
cards.notes: Disable both ends before final geometry checks. Joining must never invent fabrication cutbacks or alter web jack/king intent.
cards.acceptance: Before commit, require joins false at both ends plus native cut within tolerance; unsupported join controls must fail visibly, not pass silently.
cards.evidence: Current prototype already disables joins; 343-member live audit

cards.title: Adopt reviewed sync safety rules and the 45-day plan
cards.notes: Reassessed both PDFs and the pasted architecture review against the current add-in. Adopt a shared JS resolver, a thin native adapter, exact source validation, persistent ownership, panel rollback and explicit recovery. Host choice remains a qualification decision.
cards.acceptance: Record adoption/defer decisions, stable card numbers, dependencies, weekend checks and day-45 release gates. This completed planning card does not claim the native safeguards have been built.
cards.evidence: Current code, Autodesk/Microsoft documentation and docs/native-handoff/FRAMING-SYNC-45-DAY-PLAN.md

cards.title: Define model, panel and member identity with baseline schema
cards.notes: Separate model lineage, current document session and file/save location. Persistent CAS member GUIDs are distinct from calculation memberKey, ElementId and display Mark. Keep current exchange identities valid until an explicit versioned migration is reviewed. DocumentVersion is revision evidence, not permanent model identity or a complete freshness gate. Position-derived SlotId values are matching hints, not persistent member GUIDs.
cards.acceptance: Define versioned schema and migrations; test copied members, copied files, Save As local copies versus intentional forks, detach and cloud identity. Preserve source wall UniqueId/panel identity without guessing by mark or nearest geometry. Specify baseline fields, precision and semantic plan/source hashes; ambiguous identity stops Apply. Test moved openings and changed stud spacing without matching by bay ordinal or rounded station alone; ambiguous remapping needs explicit review.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Block Apply when source, settings or bindings have changed
cards.notes: Modeless UI snapshots become stale. Re-read the source in the valid Revit API context immediately before each panel is applied.
cards.acceptance: Changed wall/opening geometry, transform, template/settings, family binding, document/session or supported feature version blocks the old plan. Include linked-source revision/transform where supported. Re-resolve explicitly and preview again; no clicked-through warning. Test changes after preview and between queued batches.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Design and prove panel ownership and first-creation claims
cards.notes: Prefer panel-scoped baseline/receipt storage over a routinely edited global ProjectInformation record. A DataStorage record alone cannot prevent two users creating the first record at once.
cards.acceptance: Choose and document an enforceable panel-claim mechanism, including first creation. Check returned checkout results and source freshness; cached status is advisory. Enumerate actual writes/dependencies and fail an incomplete checkout atomically. Disconnected central stays workshared. Avoid unrelated borrowing/relinquishment; prove two-session claim contention before writer integration. Block grouped target members with a clear reason before writing; never ungroup automatically. Measure the actual borrow set, including indirect family/level/host dependencies, and prove that supported independent placement does not unexpectedly borrow source walls.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Qualify family bindings and independent physical checks
cards.notes: Reuse the calibrated facing/cut audit. Bind by actual loaded family/type behavior, role, insertion datum and physical section; a rotation parameter or FacingOrientation alone is insufficient.
cards.acceptance: Qualify supported C/T categories and recipes with independent solids/axes. Verify both ends disjoined, exact physical cuts and established web top-gap datum (gap replaces top cutback; no added web thickness). Use unrounded measurements with justified tolerances, preserving frozen fabrication outputs. Family reload/retype or axis/config changes invalidate affected caches. Reject unknown bindings. Include inactive family types, nested GeometryInstances and modified instances returning top-level solids. Separate physical measurement from reference-based annotation; traverse actual geometry and transforms. End reversal is not proof of correct cross-section facing.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Qualify host and exact Revit runtime before choosing UI shell
cards.notes: Compare a read-only local WebView2 CasWindow with a separate companion if embedding fails. No dockable WebView2. No privileged bridge to the public Pages site. Neither architecture is assumed crash-proof.
cards.acceptance: Inventory actual Revit patches/runtime/add-ins early, starting with the available R23 test host. Test open/close, Home, Manage Links, Load Family, document switching and normal add-in coexistence. Include .NET 10 builds 2025.5/2026.5 when deployed. Record measured stability and deployment tradeoffs, choose a shell and list excluded hosts. No global runtime registry pinning or blanket framework retarget.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Make retries idempotent with in-model operation receipts
cards.notes: Operation IDs and immutable request hashes distinguish retry from a changed command. Local logs are diagnostic; model receipts commit with the same member/baseline changes. Reuse existing JSONL diagnostics with correlated operation/panel IDs, immutable request hash, intent, verified commit and acknowledgment stages. Logs record observations, not a second authoritative model or automatic restore source; avoid full model snapshots in diagnostic logs.
cards.acceptance: Same ID plus same payload returns an applied result only after current-state reconciliation; changed payload with that ID is rejected. Lost acknowledgment, duplicate queue events, Undo/Redo and missing receipts cannot duplicate members. Distinguish committed-in-session, saved and synchronized states. No SQLite dependency required for the first implementation.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Preview web and native edits against the last applied baseline
cards.notes: Compare baseline, current Revit state and requested web plan. Native moves, deletes, retypes and copied ownership must not be silently overwritten or adopted.
cards.acceptance: Show adds/updates/deletes and unresolved conflicts by stable identity. Default to review for native drift. Explicitly adopt a native edit into a new resolved plan or restore the reviewed plan; reconcile cut lists/quantities before release. Test changes on one side, both sides, manual delete/recreate and ambiguous matches. Do not transfer edits by stud order or nearest geometry.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Prove rollback, failure handling and Undo for one panel
cards.notes: Sunday technical checkpoint on a disposable model. A successful mock is insufficient for an Apply writer.
cards.acceptance: Inject mid-panel failure, unsupported join control and final verification mismatch: zero partial members/receipts remain. Undo and Redo restore geometry plus ownership/baseline. Check commit-time changes while a containing group can still roll back. Expected warnings are narrowly classified; unknown errors stop. Regeneration corruption aborts the whole job without further document reads or automatic retry.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Implement owned-member Update without duplicate framing
cards.notes: Extend the verified single-panel path to explicit updates, retaining stable identity and native references wherever possible.
cards.acceptance: Repeat unchanged Apply with zero new members. Update moved openings and template details with a reviewed diff, delete only proven CAS-owned items, and preserve/revalidate tags and dimensions. Vendor/MWF members and p_*/BIMSF_* values remain untouched. Native drift and ambiguous copies require resolution. Verify same quantities and output plan after every update.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Reconcile crashes, lost acknowledgments and reopened models
cards.notes: Revit commit is not disk save or central synchronization. Treat journal state as a hint and inspect the actual reopened model before retrying.
cards.acceptance: Test lost response, UI crash, host termination before commit, after commit before save, after save and after sync in disposable files. Restart validates document lineage/session, receipt, baseline and actual members. Unsaved changes lost on reopen are not reported durable; safe retry recreates only missing intended work. Undo/Redo and Save As/fork paths stay consistent. Also test unavailable or truncated JSONL and a matching receipt whose members were subsequently edited or deleted. Report diagnostic failure clearly; never acknowledge success from a stamp or log alone.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Run two-user worksharing acceptance including first creation
cards.notes: Sunday technical checkpoint using two independent user sessions and a disposable central model. If a second session is unavailable, keep the gate open.
cards.acceptance: Race first creation on one panel, edit the same panel, and edit different panels. Prove no duplicate ownership records or half assemblies. Exercise partial checkout, stale central changes, reload latest, sync failure and disconnected central. Respect existing user loans; modified/new elements need normal sync before release. Record clean blocks and confirm unrelated panels remain usable. Include grouped targets and a source wall already owned by the other user. Capture before/after ownership of source walls, panel metadata and members; prove the documented claim policy without unexpected wall borrowing or automatic ungrouping.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Add bounded panel batches with stop and resume
cards.notes: Large jobs use short ExternalEvent slices with closed transactions at every yield. Start conservatively and tune from measurements.
cards.acceptance: Keep each payload below consumer limits, validate partitions and cap any oversized panel explicitly. Progress counts completed/verified work. Stop at the next panel boundary, retain verified panels, mark the rest unattempted, and resume idempotently. Never hold a transaction/group across callbacks or await. State multiple Undo actions honestly; automatic whole-job compensation is deferred.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Measure and tune collection, calibration and cache costs
cards.notes: Separate pure web calculation, serialization, Revit placement, regeneration and verification costs. The existing mock is a baseline, not a throughput promise.
cards.acceptance: Collect relevant instances/types once per validated snapshot; reuse bounded caches only with document/family/axis/settings invalidation. Avoid per-member collectors and unconditional regeneration. Record elapsed time, peak memory and UI delay for cold/warm repeated templates and mixed panels. Choose batch limits from evidence, not fixed 25-panel/2-MiB/one-regeneration claims. Measure inactive-type activation and nested/direct-solid traversal separately; activate each required inactive type in a valid transaction and recheck after reload/retype. Cache numeric results or DTOs with invalidation, not live Revit geometry across callbacks.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Verify local assets, bridge security and document lifecycle
cards.notes: Qualify the selected host with the actual shared web UI. Packaged HTML alone does not make PDF/OCR offline.
cards.acceptance: Cold-cache network-disabled test of approved bundled scripts/workers/WASM/language assets and licenses. Narrow command allowlist; validate origin or authenticated IPC peer, nonce, document, schema and limits. Reject hostile navigation/frames, old sessions and document switching. Scope drafts per model; global preferences stay separate. Verify 100/150/200% DPI, keyboard, clipboard, save, close/reopen and no cross-document writes.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Review conflicts and two-user messages in plain language
cards.notes: Saturday owner checkpoint, 30 minutes after implementation. Check whether a detailer understands what will change and why a panel is blocked.
cards.acceptance: Move/delete/retype one generated member, change an opening, and encounter a borrowed panel. Verify the preview identifies the exact conflict without losing edits, offers explicit next steps and never changes another user's members. Record confusing wording and confirm the native-edit resolution policy.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Rehearse stop, restart and recovery without duplicates
cards.notes: Sunday owner checkpoint, 30 minutes. Use disposable files and the prepared recovery harness.
cards.acceptance: Start a bounded batch, stop at a panel boundary, reopen the workspace and resume. Compare completed/remaining counts. Review saved versus unsaved crash outcomes and Undo/Redo. User can identify what is already in the model and what remains without guessing. No automatic retry on corruption.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Package a versioned DEV pilot with output parity
cards.notes: Pin the shared web bundle to the native release. Public website updates must not silently change the privileged Revit workspace.
cards.acceptance: Install/uninstall on a clean test machine with a recorded supported runtime. Verify manifest/bundle versions, startup diagnostics, current document context and modeless host. Export the same resolved plan, one sheet per panel and shared QR/plain labels with locked Panel/Mark/Qty. Keep unsupported hosts/features disabled with clear reasons. Record the DEV pilot artifact and its dependency closure. Any later production promotion must use qualified source and resources without shipping or depending on the DEV add-in. Verify Revit API references are not copied into the payload; retain the shared JS resolver and record the exact native patch plus web-bundle version.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Triage later architecture options from pilot evidence
cards.notes: Deferred: SQLite/WAL job database, automatic multi-slice compensating rollback, generic orphan geometry matching, global runtime pinning and unsupported geometry expansion. These are not prerequisites for the bounded pilot. AssemblyLoadContext isolation is also deferred unless a reproduced dependency collision justifies a scoped design and host tests; it is not a blanket guarantee for native browser conflicts.
cards.acceptance: Keep deferred unless pilot measurements demonstrate a concrete need and a separately reviewed design. Record any future proposal with risk, benefit and acceptance tests. No silent adoption of report recommendations or dependency installations.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Publish the tested support matrix and recovery runbook
cards.notes: Make the handoff usable by a detailer and support person. Document exact host patch/runtime/family/recipe evidence and known restrictions.
cards.acceptance: Include reproducible load/refresh/compare/apply/update steps, saved-versus-unsaved recovery, stop/resume and Undo scope. Document central ownership conflicts, identity forks and source/plan version checks. Keep private model data out of diagnostics. Only verified combinations enter the support matrix.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

cards.title: Resolve pilot findings or narrow the release scope
cards.notes: Reserved correction and retest buffer. A failing gate moves the relevant card back to In progress; dates do not waive safety checks.
cards.acceptance: Close reproducible pilot defects with targeted tests and actual host evidence. Rerun affected regressions and update limits. If a gate cannot pass, explicitly exclude that host/recipe/workflow or extend its date before #006 sign-off.
cards.evidence: Planned acceptance; not implemented or host-qualified

plan.summary: 45-day pilot plan. Weekend checkpoints included. Dates are targets; prerequisites and recorded evidence decide readiness.
